paper.author: Patrick Lopatto

numbered_results.label: thm:main
numbered_results.semantic_statement: Full RSB at every beta > 1: the actual unique Parisi minimizer is supported on [0,q], q in (0,1), and equals a nonnegative density smooth up to both endpoints on [0,q), plus an atom c in (0,1) at q.
semantic_cautions: Actual minimizer existence and uniqueness; genuine measure decomposition and topological support; all-order one-sided smooth density, not just an interior smoothness assertion.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion

numbered_results.label: thm:atom
numbered_results.semantic_statement: For m=1-c, m*(4-m+1/(beta^2*q)) <= 2, and c > max(sqrt(2)-1, 1-2*beta^2*q).
semantic_cautions: Left mass alpha(q-) is used; alpha(q)=1 is different. Both lower bounds are strict, including when one lower bound is negative.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion

numbered_results.label: prop:PDE-regularity
numbered_results.semantic_statement: Every probability measure has an even Parisi potential with jointly continuous positive spatial derivatives, uniform-in-measure bounds of every order, |u_x|<=1 and 0<u_xx<=1. Weak convergence of measures yields global uniform convergence of every spatial derivative, including order zero.
semantic_cautions: Global beta>0. Bounds K_j depend only on beta and j, not the measure. Order-zero potentials are unbounded, but their differences have a finite uniform norm. Classical time differentiability is not claimed at arbitrary CDF jumps.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion

numbered_results.label: lem:comparison
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{lem:comparison}
Let $T>0$, $K\ge0$, and $I=\R$ or $I=[0,\infty)$. Let
$v\in C([0,T]\times I)\cap C^{1,2}((0,T]\times I^\circ)$ be bounded
and satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:comparison-ineq}
 v_t-\frac12v_{xx}-bv_x-\kappa v\ge0
 \qquad\text{on }(0,T]\times I^\circ,
\end{equation}
where $b(t,x)\operatorname{sgn}(x)\le K$ and $\kappa\le K$.
If $v(0,\cdot)\ge0$ and, when $I=[0,\infty)$, $v(t,0)\ge0$, then
$v\ge0$ on $[0,T]\times I$.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: Bounded classical supersolutions on R or the half-line are nonnegative if nonnegative initially and at the half-line boundary, assuming only a bound on the outward drift component and an upper zeroth-order coefficient bound.
semantic_cautions: Outward condition b(t,x)*sgn(x)<=K is weaker than a two-sided drift bound. Maximum principle must retain the half-line case and time terminal one-sided interpretation.

numbered_results.label: rem:slope
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{rem:slope}
The meaning of \Cref{prop:backward} in terms of the magnetization $B=u_x$,
described in \Cref{s:outline}, rests on the following computation. On an
interval
$[q_0,q_1)$ where $\alpha_\nu=m$, we write the Parisi equation in the backward time
$\tau=\beta^2(q_1-s)$, so that $u_\tau=\frac12(u_{xx}+mu_x^2)$, and we let
$\chi(\tau,B)$ be the susceptibility $u_{xx}$ at the point $x(\tau,B)$
where $u_x=B$. Differentiating at fixed $B$, we find that
\[
 \partial_\tau\chi=\chi^2\Bigl(\frac12\chi_{BB}+m\Bigr),
 \qquad
 \partial_\tau x=z-mB,
 \qquad
 \partial_\tau\log\chi=-Q,
 \qquad
 \partial_B\partial_\tau\sqrt\chi=\frac{H_x}{4\sqrt\chi},
\]
together with $z=-\frac12\chi_B$ and $Q=-\chi(\frac12\chi_{BB}+m)$. Hence,
at fixed magnetization and along the backward evolution, the inequality
$z\ge mB$ for $B\ge0$ means that the position $x$ moves outward, $Q\ge0$
means that the susceptibility decreases, and $H_x\ge0$ means that the slope
$\partial_B\sqrt\chi\le0$ increases. In the forward time $t=\beta^2s$, the
first identity reads $\partial_t\chi=Q\chi$, which is \eqref{e:chipde}.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: At fixed magnetization B, backward susceptibility/field derivatives satisfy chi_tau=chi^2*(chi_BB/2+m), x_tau=z-m*B, log chi_tau=-Q, and d_B d_tau sqrt chi=H_x/(4 sqrt chi), with z=-chi_B/2 and Q=-chi*(chi_BB/2+m).
semantic_cautions: This is substantive coordinate calculus, not only a literature remark. Actual inverse magnetization must exist for B in (-1,1), with genuine time/spatial differentiability. Forward rescaled time reverses the signs.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion
formalized_parts: Actual inverse magnetization and susceptibility identities, with genuine time and spatial derivatives on the constant-CDF interior.

numbered_results.label: lem:heat-step
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{lem:heat-step}
Let $0<r<t$, and suppose that $\nu$ is finitely supported with no atom in
$(r/\beta^2,t/\beta^2)$. We take the value of $w(r,\cdot)$ after a possible
atom at $r/\beta^2$ and the value of $w(t,\cdot)$ before a possible atom
at $t/\beta^2$, and let $Z$ be a standard Gaussian variable. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:heat-step}
 w(t,x)=-\log\E\exp\left[-w\left(r,
       \frac rt x+\sqrt{\frac{r(t-r)}t}\,Z\right)\right]
 \qquad\text{for all } x\in\R.
\end{equation}
Further, $w(t,\cdot)$ is even for every $t>0$.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: The actual finite-atomic correction after a heat step obeys the exact log Gaussian expectation with mean (r/t)*x and variance r*(t-r)/t; it is even.
semantic_cautions: 0<r<t and no atoms inside the rescaled interval. The value at r is after its atom, and at t before its possible atom.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion
numbered_results.coverage_note: Statement_4_2 contains the bridge heat-step identity, extended from finite atomic measures to arbitrary measures with zero open-interval mass. The separate final evenness sentence is supplied by forwardBridgeCorrection_even and forwardBridgeLeftCorrection_even, and also by the density/gauge conclusions of Proposition 4.1.

numbered_results.label: lem:forward-derivative-bounds
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{lem:forward-derivative-bounds}
For every $k\ge1$, there exists a constant $c_k>0$ depending only on
$\beta$ and $k$ such that
\[
 |\partial_x^jw(t,x)|\le c_k
 \qquad\text{for all } t\in(0,\beta^2],\ x\in\R,\ \text{and } 1\le j\le k.
\]
This holds for both one-sided values at the atoms of $\nu$.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: All positive spatial derivatives up to any order of the finite-atomic correction are bounded uniformly in measure/time/space, including both one-sided atom values.
semantic_cautions: Product constants are controlled by the total atomic mass, not by the number of atoms. Actual nonlinear Gaussian convolution derivatives and log-ratio identities are needed.

numbered_results.label: rem:weighted-law
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{rem:weighted-law}
We translate \Cref{lem:transport} into the magnetization coordinate of
\Cref{s:outline}. Since $B_x=C>0$, let $x(t,b)$ be the field satisfying
$B(t,x(t,b))=b$ for a fixed magnetization $b$.
The identity $\mathcal DB=0$ gives
$\partial_t x(t,b)=v(t,x(t,b))$, so the chain rule identifies
$(\mathcal DF)(t,x(t,b))$ with the partial time derivative
of $F(t,x(t,b))$ with $b$ held fixed, where $F$ is any smooth function. Let $r=pC$, viewed as a function of $t$ and
$B$. Since $\dd B=C\dd x$, the density of $M_s=u_x(s,X_s)$ is $p/C$, so
that $r=\chi^2(p/C)$ and $\omega\dd x=2r\dd B$. In particular, the image of $\rho$
under $u_x$ has density proportional to $r$ on $[0,1)$. Since
$\omega=2rC$, the identity \eqref{eq:weight-transport} together with
$\mathcal D\log C=Q$ and $v_x=-Q$ gives $\mathcal D\log r=K/2-Q-H$. Next,
$(\log r)_x=(\log p)_x+(\log C)_x=-(N+z)$, so that
$N+z=-\chi\,\partial_B\log r$. Differentiating once more with
$\partial_B=C^{-1}\partial_x$ and $C_x=-2Cz$, we find
$\frac12\chi^2r_{BB}/r=\frac12(N^2-z^2-N_x-z_x)$, and
\eqref{eq:basic-derivatives} shows that this equals $K/2-3Q-H$.
Comparing with $\mathcal D\log r$, we find that
$\mathcal Dr=\frac12\chi^2r_{BB}+2Qr$, which is \eqref{e:weighted-law}.
The formulas for $N_x$ and $z_x$ in \eqref{eq:basic-derivatives} give
$K=(N^2-N_x)+(z^2+z_x)$. Finally, since $\omega=2rC$ and
$\partial_x=C\,\partial_B$, the identity \eqref{eq:crossing-centered-identity}
reads $-\partial_B(\chi zr)/r=\Phi+\Psi$.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: The actual magnetization inverse changes field derivatives into fixed-magnetization derivatives. The actual magnetization density is p/C, its C^2-reweighted density r=p*C, and r obeys r_t=(chi^2/2)*r_BB+2Qr plus the displayed log-rate and centered identity.
semantic_cautions: This numbered remark contains mathematical identities requiring proofs. Jacobian C and half-line factor 2 must both be tracked.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion
numbered_results.coverage_note: The displayed concrete inverse-coordinate, density, Jacobian, PDE, score and centering identities are formalized. The general prose chain-rule observation for every smooth function F is not separately exposed as a universal-F theorem; its displayed concrete applications are proved.

numbered_results.label: lem:crossing-decay
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{lem:crossing-decay}
For every compact interval $J\subset\beta^2I$, there exists a constant
$c_J>0$ such that
\[
 \omega+|\omega_t|+|(\Phi\omega)_t|\le c_J(1+x^2)\e^{x-x^2/(2\beta^2)}
 \qquad\text{for all } t\in J \text{ and } x\ge0.
\]
Further, the functions $v,z,\Phi,\Phi_x,\mathcal D\Phi,H$ are bounded on
$J\times[0,\infty)$, and $v=z=0$ at $x=0$.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: On compact rescaled time subintervals, omega, its time derivative and the Phi-omega time derivative satisfy the exact polynomial times Gaussian envelope; all listed auxiliary fields are bounded, with v=z=0 at x=0.
semantic_cautions: The compact interval must lie strictly inside positive rescaled times. The displayed envelope is sufficient for differentiation and all later improper integration-by-parts boundaries.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion

numbered_results.label: cor:Gamma-prime-shape
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{cor:Gamma-prime-shape}
Let $\nu,I,m$ be as in \Cref{prop:crossing}. There exists $s_*$ in the
closure of $I$ such that $\Gamma_\nu'$ is strictly decreasing on
$I\cap(0,s_*]$ and strictly increasing on $I\cap[s_*,1)$.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: There is a turning point in the closure of each nonempty constant-positive-mass interval such that actual Gamma prime is strictly decreasing before it and strictly increasing after it, with either piece allowed empty.
semantic_cautions: The proof uses the all-time positive covariance identity, not merely the zero-crossing implication without a separate analysis theorem. Empty intervals cannot be admitted because their closure has no point.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion

numbered_results.label: rem:AC-regularity
numbered_results.statement_latex:
\label{rem:AC-regularity}
Auffinger and Chen proved that if $(a,b)\subset\supp\mu_P$ for a Parisi
measure $\mu_P$ of a mixed $p$-spin model, then its distribution function
is infinitely differentiable on the half-open interval $[a,b)$
\cite[Theorem~2(ii)]{AuffingerChenProperties}. Their proof uses the first
identity in \eqref{eq:quotient}, followed by the same differentiation of
moments used above. Applied with $(a,b)=(0,q_\beta)$, as allowed by
\Cref{prop:connected-support}, their theorem gives smoothness on
$[0,q_\beta)$. The additional point here is that continuity of every
polynomial moment at $q_\beta$, together with the moment
identities and the quotient formula, allows the same
induction to give derivatives of every order up to that
endpoint.
numbered_results.semantic_statement: The cited earlier mixed-p-spin interior/half-open regularity theorem supplies smoothness below q; the present moment/quotient induction strengthens the actual SK result to all derivative orders at q.
semantic_cautions: The historical theorem for every mixed model is cited background; the paper-specific endpoint improvement is a substantive proved claim.
global_hypotheses: actual Parisi potential and actual zero-initial optimal diffusion
numbered_results.coverage_note: The paper’s SK conclusion, including all-order one-sided endpoint regularity, is proved. The preceding quoted Auffinger–Chen theorem for general mixed-p-spin models is separately recorded as cited background; the project does not claim a general mixed-model theorem.

semantic_scope.smooth_closed_interval: The paper defines C-infinity([0,q]) as interior smoothness with continuous extensions of every derivative to both endpoints. Time derivatives at 0 and q are one-sided; the discontinuous actual CDF at q is not asserted smooth.
semantic_scope.support: Topological support of the actual Borel probability measure on [0,1], identified with its real image, not the set of atoms.
semantic_scope.density: A chosen smooth positive density representing the actual selected optimal diffusion law at each s>0; identities for arbitrary densities do not prove the physical targets.
semantic_scope.weak_approximation: Convergence in the weak topology of probability measures, not convergence assumed in a stronger bespoke metric.
semantic_scope.SDE_realization: Projective Gaussian probability space BrownianSample = nonnegative-real times to real values, carrying an everywhere-continuous Brownian modification and its natural filtration. The Wiener measure on continuous paths is a pushforward. Actual strong pathwise diffusion; stochastic identities use canonical adapted uniform left sums at each fixed terminal time, with L2 or in-measure convergence. No usual augmentation, arbitrary-filtration, or arbitrary-partition theorem is asserted.
semantic_scope.numbered_target_correspondence: The closed numbered targets include stronger variants and auxiliary identities. The explicit slope sign in Remark 3.2 and the evenness sentence in Lemma 4.2 have additional declaration mappings. Remark 5.3 does not separately expose its generic chain-rule paragraph as a universal-function theorem.
semantic_scope.proof_status: A proposition-valued target is a definition; a corresponding theorem is a supplied proof declaration. Source classifications are distinct from fresh compilation, transitive-axiom auditing, and independent kernel verification of a specific source revision.
